title: When service has to be rescued from performance
issueStatement: The work may still be happening, but the heart has started bargaining for identity, recognition, or emotional reward in return.
centralInsight: Gurbani binds seva to humility, truthful labor, and offering. Service becomes holy when it stops feeding the self that performs it.
practicalReflection: Seva is not merely doing good things. It is learning to serve without secretly turning the service back toward self-advertisement.
actionPrompt: Ask where your service is still asking to be seen, thanked, or emotionally repaid, and loosen your grip there first.

daily.label: Daily
daily.title: Service in the work already in front of you
daily.issueStatement: You may be waiting for obviously spiritual work while overlooking the ordinary labor, care, and attention that could already become service.
daily.centralInsight: The Guru does not separate seva from daily work so quickly. Fidelity in the ordinary can also be offering.
daily.practicalReflection: The day is full of chances to serve without announcement. The difficulty is that they often look small and unremarkable.
daily.actionPrompt: Turn one necessary task today into service by doing it cleanly, quietly, and without inward complaint.

pressure.label: Under Pressure
pressure.title: Service when urgency steals tenderness
pressure.issueStatement: Under pressure, service can become efficient but loveless, dutiful but impatient, helpful but spiritually empty.
pressure.centralInsight: Gurbani refuses to let urgency become an excuse for losing humility. True service keeps its center even when the pace rises.
pressure.practicalReflection: Pressure reveals whether you were serving the person, the task, or your own idea of usefulness.
pressure.actionPrompt: In the next demanding moment, do the needed work without letting haste strip away gentleness.

repair.label: After the Slip
repair.title: Returning when service became self-serving
repair.issueStatement: You can feel that the work drifted toward ego, resentment, or control, but the mind would rather blame the people around you than face that drift.
repair.centralInsight: Repair in seva begins with motive, not image. The Guru brings the heart back to offering before it redesigns the appearance of service.
repair.practicalReflection: It is possible to keep serving outwardly while the inward act has already soured. Honest repair addresses that inward souring directly.
repair.actionPrompt: Confess where service became about self, then do one hidden act of care that earns you nothing back.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: Training the heart for real seva
practice.issueStatement: A single generous act is easier than becoming a person whose habits, timing, and ego are actually shaped by service.
practice.centralInsight: Seva becomes durable when humility is practiced repeatedly enough that service no longer needs applause to continue.
practice.practicalReflection: To train in seva is to let the self lose some of its appetite for credit while the hands stay available.
practice.actionPrompt: Commit to one recurring act of service that stays mostly unseen and let its hiddenness become part of the training.
